tagline: Nearly the length of Arkansas, oil country to the Ozarks.
intro: Scenic 7 starts at the Louisiana line in pine and cypress country, where oil came in near El Dorado in 1921, and runs about 290 miles north to Harrison. Past Camden, near Arkadelphia, it enters the Ouachitas, the only mountains in the country whose ridges run west to east, and winds through the Ouachita National Forest.

Then it crosses the Arkansas River valley at Dardanelle and Russellville, with Mount Nebo off to the west, and climbs again into the Ozarks, where it twists sharply and is popular with motorcyclists. It was the state's first scenic byway.
season: The Forest Service notes the byway especially for its fall color.

moments.title: Bathhouse Row
moments.text: In Hot Springs the highway passes in front of the row's eight bathhouses, some built directly over the springs the federal government set aside in 1832.

moments.title: Grand Canyon of the Ozarks
moments.text: The road wends beside this vista just before it reaches the small town square at Jasper, near the Buffalo National River.

moments.title: Harrison
moments.text: Brick storefronts under awnings and hanging baskets line a downtown square anchored by the Boone County Courthouse and the restored 1929 Hotel Seville, where the byway ends.
